title: SETA symposium speech on the presidential system
clean_text:
My dear brothers and sisters, I congratulate the administrators of SETA for organizing this symposium at a time when Türkiye stands on the eve of a historic decision to transition to the Presidential System.

Every country has a form of government unique to its own circumstances. When we look at our country, we see that over the past 200 years we have gone through many different experiences one after another.

My brothers and sisters, throughout this process our country has been worn down and diminished by wars and has paid very heavy prices. The Victory of Çanakkale represents the point at which we could no longer endure any further. Drawing inspiration and strength from Çanakkale, we fought our War of Independence.

While European countries chose to maintain monarchy alongside democracy, we sent the dynasty out of the country and proclaimed the Republic. First, we had a single-party system—please pay attention to this—and then a multi-party system of government, through which our country has reached the present day.

Since our transition to multi-party political life in 1950, we have always tried to keep our democracy standing under the shadow of military coups and tutelary administrations.

The most important consequence of these distortions has been the constant threat to an environment of stability and confidence. Political instability also brings economic and social problems with it.

Our search over the past 200 years, our experiences during the Republican era, and especially what we have gone through in recent years show us one reality: if we want to achieve our goals as a country and as a nation, we first need a strong and effective system of government in which it is completely clear who holds authority and responsibility.

In fact, the Presidential System that we are discussing today did not suddenly emerge in a day, a month, or a year. Behind it lies such a deep and thought-provoking historical background.

The system we are discussing is the most appropriate solution to the question of survival that Türkiye and the Turkish nation have faced for centuries. That is the issue.

When we bring together all these experiences, the events we have lived through, and our reading of history, our country's need for a new constitution and, along with it, a new system of government becomes as clear as day. My brothers and sisters, as you can see, the Presidential System we are discussing today has nothing to do with the regime, one-man rule, or personalization of power.

The issue is our effort, as a country and a nation, to establish a system of government that is much stronger, much more resilient, and much better suited to achieving our goals in light of the experiences we have had in the past.

The greatest safeguard of the Presidential System is that it is democratic in the true sense of the word. Under this system, no one who fails to win the support of more than half of our nation can have the opportunity to govern the country.

What we are engaged in here is a struggle over a system. This is a struggle over the system. What will happen after Erdoğan? Whatever the nation says will happen. Whatever God wills will happen.

More importantly, Türkiye has already taken its first steps toward this system and has successfully completed them. I am referring to the constitutional amendment of 2007.

Therefore, with the constitutional amendment, rather than personalizing the issue, we are placing governance within a system.

My brothers and sisters, without a soul, the body is merely a corpse. Likewise, if we do not explain to our nation the spirit, essence, and fundamental meaning of this issue, the provisions of the constitutional amendment alone will remain nothing more than dry legal expressions.

With this understanding, until the date of the referendum, until April 16, those of us who say “Yes” to the Presidential System of Government must travel across every corner of our country, use every means of communication, and explain the new system.

Why? Yes for one nation. Yes for one flag. Yes for one homeland. Yes for one state.

The essence of the Presidential System is that the authority to govern is given directly to the nation.

Because the President, who will perform the executive function, will be accountable to the nation from whom he derives his authority, he will have to act at every step knowing that the eyes of the public are upon him.

What did we say? Ours will be a Turkish-style Presidential System. We do not have to be exactly the same as others.

The President—that is, the head of the executive—will represent the executive branch. He will form his cabinet, appoint its members, and dismiss them when necessary. But to whom will he be accountable? He will be accountable to the nation. He will be accountable to the nation.

The executive branch, which currently has two heads—the President and the Prime Minister—will now be united under a single office. In this way, from the very beginning, our nation will know to whom it has given authority, who has assumed responsibility, and therefore whom it can hold accountable when necessary.

The legislative body and the members of parliament serving there will focus solely on their primary duties under the new system.

With the new system, which clearly separates the executive from the legislature, all members of parliament will be able to concentrate on parliamentary work.

title: New Year message 2022/23
clean_text:
My Dear Nation,

I greet each and every one of you with my warmest feelings and deepest affection.

Today, we are not only bringing one year to a close and welcoming a new one; we are also entering a period in which we will leave behind the first century of our Republic and step into its new century.

We began the centennial commemorations of the National Struggle in Samsun in 2019.

In fact, we had hoped that, together, we would celebrate with great enthusiasm every centennial anniversary of the events that took place during the four-year period leading up to the proclamation of the Republic.

We had also made very serious preparations for this.

However, the measures implemented within the framework of the COVID-19 pandemic forced us to mark this period with more modest commemorative ceremonies.

So much so that, even on the 100th anniversary of the opening of the Grand National Assembly, we had to make do with messages of congratulations.

Praise be to God, we have left those difficult days behind us.

God willing, we will be able to celebrate the joy of the 100th anniversary of the founding of our Republic on October 29, 2023, with the enthusiasm we had envisioned.

Moreover, 2023 also marks the milestone of a promise we made to our nation 12 years ago.

Since the 2011 elections, when we presented our 2023 goals—one of the most ambitious visions for democracy and development in our country—to the judgment of our nation and received its approval, we have worked day and night to fulfill this promise.

The events that began immediately after Türkiye announced its 2023 goals and have continued without interruption until today are, in one respect, an indication of how many centers of power we unsettled with this step.

From the Gezi events of 2013 to the December 17–25 police-judiciary coup attempt that same year…

From the PKK’s trench operations to DAESH’s harassment of our borders…

From the attempted coup of July 15, 2016, to the international sabotage targeting our economy in 2018…

Throughout this critical period, in which we were subjected to countless attacks from all sides, we never took a step back from our 2023 goals while simultaneously carrying out a multifaceted struggle.

On the contrary;

By strengthening our national unity and solidarity…

By expanding our counterterrorism strategy in the direction of eliminating threats at their source…

By burying terrorists in the trenches they had dug…

By crushing the coup plotters…

By frustrating economic hitmen through our own programs…

By mobilizing our country’s resources at full capacity in order to turn global crises into opportunities…

In short, by struggling together with all our strength, we have always continued on our path under the guidance of our 2023 goals.

Without a doubt, the economic difficulties that began in the final months of 2021 and continued throughout 2022 have troubled all of us.

The negative developments around the world, which struggled to withstand the economic shock caused first by the global pandemic and then by the Russia-Ukraine war, inevitably affected us as well.

However, during this period, the most important feature distinguishing Türkiye from the rest of the world, particularly from developed countries, has been its economic model, which refuses to compromise on employment and production.

Yes, this country has experienced a rise in the cost of living.

But everyone with a conscience will acknowledge that, during the same period, this country also reached the highest employment level, the highest production capacity, and the highest export figures in its history.

In other words, we did not leave our nation alone in the face of the rising cost of living, nor did we abandon our people to their fate.

Instead;

We increased employment so that everyone could earn an income…

We tried to compensate for the loss of welfare experienced by workers through substantial increases…

We continuously supported industry and commerce so that the wheels of the economy would keep turning.

If Türkiye today is still standing tall despite all the attacks it has endured and all the crises that have swept across the world, we owe this to the determined struggle we have waged and to the distinctive political and economic policies we have pursued.

No one can deny the reality of a Türkiye that, through its sensible, composed, peace-oriented and moderate stance in international crises, has earned the respect of everyone, including its longstanding adversaries.

While the world has been grappling with an energy crisis, through our own discoveries and through our position as a center of international supply and trade routes, we have placed ourselves in a different position.

We have progressed from the days when terrorist organizations’ attacks targeting our cities were turned into an instrument of blackmail against our country to a level at which we are able to conduct operations dozens, and sometimes hundreds, of kilometers beyond our borders.

Wherever we travel in our country, we see hundreds of factories under construction, being opened, and shipping goods intensively both domestically and abroad.

In tourism, we have not only compensated for our losses, but are also concluding a season in which we reached the highest level of revenue in our history.

Whichever field you look at, you will see similar pictures.

I would like to underline and repeat once again that we are closing 2022, just like the past 20 years, with gains greater than the difficulties we have faced.

God willing, in 2023, with our Türkiye Century vision, we will launch a much greater breakthrough in our country, one worthy of the new century of our Republic.

Our goal is no longer merely to enter the highest tier of the global political and economic league.

Our goal is to attain the political and economic power necessary to take our place among the very top ranks of that highest tier.

We regard the infrastructure of democracy and development that we have brought to our country over the past 20 years as the foundation, the beginning, the “Bismillah” of this great leap forward.

In other words, we are only just beginning.

Our aim is to make this beginning in the best and most effective way possible and to leave our young people a country in which they can carry the Türkiye Century to success in a manner consistent with our goals, our dreams, and our civilizational and historical heritage.

With these feelings, I bid farewell to 2022 and wish every member of our nation, and all of humanity, a 2023 filled with peace, tranquility, prosperity, and well-being.

May God protect you.

Stay well and in good health…

title: New Year message 2023/24
clean_text:
My Dear Nation,

I greet each and every one of you with my most heartfelt feelings and affection.

Tonight, we are bringing the year 2023 to a close and stepping into 2024.

I wish for the new calendar year to bring goodness to our country, our nation, and all of humanity.

In fact, we believe that every new year should be welcomed with joy, hope, and excitement.

However, we are entering this new year with a sense of sorrow, both because of the adverse developments in our region and around the world, and because of the martyrs we lost in recent days.

Of course, we continue to preserve our hope for a better, more peaceful, and more prosperous future for all of humanity.

For this to happen, first of all, we need to see the so-called democratic and freedom-loving countries cease their support for terrorist organizations with blood on their hands.

For this to happen, first of all, we need to see all countries and institutions take a common stance against the killing of innocent children and women in Gaza.

For this to happen, first of all, we need to see fair and sincere efforts being made to bring an end to conflicts, particularly the Russia-Ukraine war, which inflict suffering on individuals and squander the resources of countries.

For this to happen, first of all, we need to see the wealth of societies that have been exploited for centuries and whose dignity has been trampled upon being used for their own future, prosperity, and security.

In short, in order to turn hopes into reality, we need to ensure that all countries, institutions, and individuals around the world unite around common values and principles.

As Türkiye, we represent a different place, a different mission, and a different understanding in this global picture.

As a state and as a nation, we are not merely striving to bring our own efforts for security and prosperity to fruition.

With the understanding that we ourselves cannot find peace unless an atmosphere of peace prevails in our region and throughout the world, we seek the same standards for everyone.

With this understanding,

We are working to bring peace efforts in our region to fruition.

We are developing our relations with our friends in every field.

We share the troubles and concerns of our brothers and sisters.

We support every effort aimed at preparing the world for a better, fairer, and more prosperous future.

At a time when we have completed the first century of our Republic and entered its new century, which we call the Century of Türkiye, we continue to reinforce our determination and efforts as we set our sights on even greater goals.

We believe that the oppression of the oppressor will not continue forever.

We believe that the unjust and unbalanced global system of governance is going through its final struggles.

We believe that the voice of the oppressed is spreading deeply throughout the world, and that these cries will grow and turn into the common conscience of humanity.

Indeed, we see that Türkiye’s statements and positions, which address not only its own citizens, friends, and brothers and sisters but all of humanity, are increasingly finding resonance in people’s hearts.

My Dear Nation,

Of course, along this arduous path, we constantly encounter new trials, new difficulties, and new obstacles.

At the root of many of the problems we face, from the fight against terrorism to economic traps, lies the objective of preventing the construction of a great and powerful Türkiye.

As long as we, as a country, continue to use our potential and capabilities effectively, this struggle will become even tougher.

Because Türkiye’s growth means disrupting the calculations of those who, for centuries, have been able to act freely all around us thanks to our setbacks.

Our becoming stronger means bringing an end to the systems of those who use, exploit, and oppress everyone else for the sake of their own prosperity and security.

For our voice to be heard more means strengthening the pursuit of rights, justice, freedom, and conscience throughout the world.

At no point in its history has our nation shied away from paying a price, making sacrifices, or taking responsibility in order to achieve its goals.

The strong stance our nation has displayed in the face of the many critical events we have experienced over the past 21 years shows that this determination continues today.

Yes, I would like to repeat this once again from here.

As long as our nation protects its unity, solidarity, and brotherhood, with God’s permission, no one will be able to divide us.

As our state implements the Century of Türkiye vision, which is the next stage of our 2023 goals, with God’s permission, our crescent-and-star flag will continue to rise.

As we continue, through our political, economic, military, and diplomatic achievements, to inspire confidence in our friends and fear in our enemies, the fog before us will gradually clear.

In short, as long as we do not compromise our independence or our future, no one will be able to stand in the way of our blessed march.

In the past, we lost a great deal of time, energy, and human life because of tutelary forces, coup plotters, terrorist organizations, and political and social engineering projects imposed upon us as instruments of imperialists.

We have long since had enough of these schemes, and we have no intention of paying such heavy prices again.

We parted ways long ago with those who kept our country occupied with internal struggles and deprived it of its historical legacy and the opportunities it should possess.

This is precisely the meaning of the principle we repeat at every opportunity: “ONE NATION, ONE FLAG, ONE STATE, ONE HOMELAND.”

God willing, 2024 will be a year in which we leave behind the difficult period that began with the coup attempt, grew with the COVID-19 pandemic, and deepened with the conflicts in our region, and instead focus on our goals.

At a time when global crises continue to intensify, we will once again demonstrate our difference and raise the star of a Türkiye that produces, creates employment, grows, and develops.

Yes, the 2023 goals were only the beginning; our real rise begins with the Century of Türkiye and with 2024.

We sincerely believe that, with your support, we will bring this struggle to victory as well.

With these feelings, I once again wish for the new calendar year to bring goodness to every member of our nation and to all of humanity.

I greet you all with love and respect.

Stay well and healthy.

title: New Year message 2024/25
clean_text:
My Beloved Nation,

I greet you all with my heartfelt feelings and affection.

Today, we bid farewell to 2024 and welcome the year 2025 with new hopes, expectations, and dreams.

First and foremost, I pray to Almighty God that the new calendar year will bring goodness to our country, our nation, the broader geography with which we share bonds of heart and culture, and all of humanity.

I remember with mercy all our martyrs who laid down their lives for our independence and our future over the past year, and I express my gratitude to our veterans.

As a nation, God willing, we will further strengthen our unity, solidarity, and togetherness in 2025 and stand even more firmly together.

The year 2024, which we are leaving behind, witnessed many critical developments both within our country and across our region.

We successfully held our Local Administration Elections in an atmosphere of a true celebration of democracy, once again demonstrating to the entire world the maturity of Turkish democracy.

While the will of our nation was freely expressed at the ballot box, once again, alongside our democracy, all 85 million of our citizens emerged as the winners.

Regardless of their preferences, I would once again like to thank all my fellow citizens who turned the ballot boxes into places of celebration.

Despite the elections and the new crises that erupted in our region, we have begun to reap the benefits of the economic program that we have been implementing with determination.

We achieved very important successes in employment, exports, production, tourism, the defense industry, and many other fields.

We made significant progress in our efforts to rebuild and revive our earthquake-stricken regions, and these efforts will accelerate further in the new year.

The continuing decline in inflation, particularly at an increasing pace during the final months of the year, confirms that we will achieve our targets for 2025.

By giving greater priority to policies that will compensate our citizens for their loss of welfare and increase their purchasing power, God willing, we will reach much better conditions.

In 2025, we will continue with determination our fight against opportunists who seek to profit at the expense of our people through exorbitant prices, particularly in housing, rents, and food.

I especially ask my fellow citizens not to give credence to populist rhetoric that has imposed very heavy costs on Türkiye in the past.

Just as we have resolved the problems of this country and this nation over the past 22 years, we will once again overcome the current cyclical difficulties in the economy.

We are on the right path; with God's permission, we will achieve our goals.

All we ask of you is a little more patience, resilience, and understanding.

My Beloved Nation,

The final weeks of 2024 marked the beginning of a new era in Syria, a country with which we share deep-rooted historical, human, and neighborly ties.

We will provide every form of support necessary for this new era to open the way for lasting peace, tranquility, stability, and economic prosperity in Syria.

As stability takes root in Syria, I believe that the voluntary return of Syrian refugees who have longed for their homeland for the past 13 years will also become easier.

I say, “May God be pleased with you,” to all my fellow citizens who, throughout this period, displayed the finest examples of being an “Ansar Nation,” a nation that offers refuge and support.

We are the country that has given one of the strongest responses to the massacres in Gaza from the very first day and has demonstrated its conscientious and just stance on every platform.

We are making intensive efforts to bring an end to the massacres that have continued for 15 months in Gaza and the other Palestinian territories and to establish peace there as well.

In 2025, we will continue to work with all our strength for the establishment of a free, sovereign, and territorially integral Palestinian State based on the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

Bringing the war between Russia and Ukraine, both of which are our neighbors across the Black Sea, to an end through a just peace will remain one of our priorities.

Our hope is that a new era will begin to our north as well in 2025.

While carrying out all these diplomatic initiatives beyond our borders, our most important agenda at home will be the strengthening of our “home front.”

We are determined to make the Century of Türkiye a century of brotherhood.

In the period ahead, we will take determined steps to turn our vision of a “TERROR-FREE TÜRKİYE” and a “TERROR-FREE REGION” into reality.

We are making every effort to ensure that this process, which will open a new path before our country, proceeds smoothly and with mutual goodwill and understanding.

However, when necessary, we will not hesitate to bring into play the iron fist of our state inside the velvet glove.

Within this framework, we hope and desire, God willing, to bring our nation new good news in 2025.

May Almighty God be our guide and helper.

May Almighty God never let us fall short before our beloved nation, whom we are honored to serve, or before the hundreds of millions of oppressed people who have placed their hopes in Türkiye.

With these wishes, I hope that the new calendar year brings goodness to our country, our nation, and all of humanity, and I greet each and every one of you with respect.

May your new year be blessed.

Stay well and in good health.

title: New Year message 2025/26
clean_text:
My Dear Nation,

I greet you all with my most heartfelt feelings, with affection and respect.

Today, we bid farewell to 2025 and prepare to say “hello” to 2026 with renewed excitement, new hopes, and new goals.

I wish for the new calendar year to bring blessings to our country, our nation, the communities and lands to which we are bound by ties of the heart, and all humanity.

I commemorate with mercy all our heroes who were martyred, whether in our fight against terrorist organizations, drug traffickers, and urban criminals, or in the defense of the security and survival of our state.

On behalf of myself and my nation, I extend my gratitude to each and every one of our veterans, who have paid great sacrifices for the peace and well-being of our 86 million citizens.

The year we have left behind witnessed important developments both in our country and around the world.

Despite the growing atmosphere of war, crises, and tensions in our region, Türkiye, under the leadership of capable and competent cadres, continues its blessed journey with confidence.

We are witnessing the positive results of the economic program we have implemented with determination across a broad range of areas.

While the disinflation process continues, the reserves of our Central Bank are growing stronger, and we are shifting into a higher gear in production, investment, employment, and exports.

From tourism to the defense industry, we continue to break record after record in many fields.

We believe that our “500,000 Social Housing Project,” for which the first draws were held two days ago, will not only enable our low-income citizens to become homeowners under highly favorable conditions, but will also contribute to reducing the excessive increases in housing and rental prices.

This year, we intend to crown the gains we have achieved in the economy with reforms.

With the support of our Parliament, God willing, we will implement step by step the Türkiye Century Reform Program that we announced at our Grand Congress.

My Esteemed Citizens,

Throughout 2025, the first priority of our government was to heal the wounds caused by the February 6 Disaster of the Century.

Although we cannot bring back the lives we lost, we have succeeded in rebuilding our cities with their infrastructure, public squares, green spaces, social facilities, and historical and cultural character.

As we promised, on December 27 in Hatay, with the participation of more than 100,000 of our brothers and sisters, we proudly handed over the key to our 455,000th earthquake home to its rightful beneficiaries.

I wish our new homes and workplaces to be auspicious and beneficial for our earthquake survivors.

I would like to thank all our brothers and sisters who, since February 6, have worked at construction sites around the clock, seven days a week, regardless of the cold of winter or the heat of summer, as well as all our institutions and benefactors who contributed to the construction of these homes.

As for those who, instead of supporting the reconstruction efforts, criticize everything that is done, I invite them to Hatay and our other disaster-stricken cities so that they can see firsthand what our state has accomplished.

As the government and the Alliance, we will continue to keep the promises we have made and, God willing, we will never let our nation down.

We will not leave alone not only our own people, but any of our brothers and sisters who look to our country for support.

The reflections of our political approach, which places rights, justice, and conscience at its core, can be seen throughout our region, particularly in Syria and Gaza.

In neighboring Syria, which attained its freedom through the December 8 Revolution, recovery has accelerated and significant progress toward political stability has been made within a short period of time.

As the atmosphere of peace in Syria has become more firmly established, voluntary returns have also increased, and over the past year 600,000 of our Syrian guests have returned to their homeland.

We believe that a strong Syria that has secured its political unity and territorial integrity will make exceptional contributions both to its region and to the world.

As Türkiye, without distinguishing between Arab, Kurd, Turkmen, Sunni, Shia, or Nusayri, we will provide the new administration with the necessary support for the peace and security of the Syrian people.

In Gaza, the ceasefire achieved with our contribution remains in place thanks to the restraint of our Gazan brothers and sisters, despite all of Israel’s violations.

We are making intensive efforts to ensure that Israel’s attacks come to an end, that the flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza accelerates, and that reconstruction efforts can begin.

Until those responsible for the deaths of 71,000 of our brothers and sisters, most of them children and women, are held accountable before justice, we will neither retreat nor remain silent, and we will never allow the genocide to be forgotten.

We also continue our initiatives to bring the Russia-Ukraine War, which is about to enter its fifth year, to an end as soon as possible through a just and lasting peace.

We are closely monitoring the growing provocations and threats directed against the interests of our country and the Turkish Cypriot people in the Eastern Mediterranean.

I would like to underline once again today that we will never tolerate faits accomplis, opportunistic encroachments, or piracy in our Blue Homeland.

My Dear Nation,

We have passed several important milestones in the Terror-Free Türkiye process, which will open an entirely new chapter not only for our country but also for our region.

As the People’s Alliance, we have always acted constructively throughout this process, focused on solutions, and put not only our hands but our entire bodies under the stone, taking full responsibility.

Our National Solidarity, Brotherhood and Democracy Commission, which has carefully listened to the relevant parties, will, God willing, soon finalize its concluding report, which we believe will give new momentum to the process.

It is our hope that the Commission will continue to act in a spirit of consensus during this final stage as well.

This process, which aims to free our country from a 40-year affliction, must not be sacrificed to the calculations of short-term political interests.

For our part, we will not hesitate to do whatever falls upon us to ensure that the process reaches its intended destination without suffering any setbacks.

Just as we have done for the past 23 years, with nothing but love for our nation and our homeland in our hearts, we will continue to serve all 86 million of our citizens and work selflessly for the prosperity, peace, and well-being of all of Türkiye.

In 2026 as well, instead of merely talking, we will produce results; instead of engaging in polemics, we will take action; and we will continue to let our works and investments speak for us.

May God be our guide and helper.

I thank everyone who supports our Türkiye Century vision.

With these thoughts, I congratulate you on the new calendar year and wish for 2026 to bring blessings to our country, our nation, our region, and all humanity.

Once again, I greet you with affection and respect.

Stay well and in good health…

title: Vœux aux Français 2023
clean_text:
My dear fellow citizens,

For the sixth time, I have the privilege of sharing this moment of New Year’s wishes with you.

With you, the officers and soldiers of our armed forces who protect us; with you, police officers, gendarmes, firefighters, security forces and sea rescuers who are keeping watch this evening. With you, doctors, healthcare workers and patients. With you, public servants who ensure the continuity of our public services. With you, citizens engaged in their professional lives or in our associations. With you, our fellow citizens overseas. With all of you who are with your families in France or abroad, and more particularly with those of you whose circumstances in life mean that you feel alone this evening. Those of you who are going through hardship, and to whom our thoughts go.

New Year’s addresses have something unique about them: they compel us to speak of a future which, in truth, we do not know, but which we know with certainty we will have to face, with our strengths and our weaknesses, but as a united country.

In carrying out the responsibilities entrusted to me, I never lose sight of this imperative of the unity of the nation that we all form together.

If we were to give in to the spirit of division that presses upon us from every side, we would have virtually no chance of overcoming the challenges before us in such a harsh world and in such difficult times. And so, for 2023, I wish for us, as far as possible, to live as a united and supportive country, recognizing the place of each person and respecting everyone.

I think back to the wishes I expressed to you at the same time one year ago. Who could have imagined then that, just as we thought we were emerging, with great difficulty, from a global pandemic, within a matter of weeks we would have to confront unimaginable challenges: war returning to European soil following Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and its democracy; tens, perhaps hundreds, of thousands of deaths; millions of refugees; a terrible energy crisis; a looming food crisis; and the invocation of the gravest threats, including nuclear ones? Who could have predicted the wave of inflation that followed? Or the climate crisis, whose dramatic effects were once again visible in our country this summer?

And yet, throughout these seasons of danger, what has remained constant, once again this year, is our collective ability to rise together to these challenges.

Yes, during this year, France, together with Europe, has upheld the voice of law and freedom in support of Ukraine; thousands of you demonstrated solidarity by welcoming into our towns and villages refugees fleeing the Russian invasion.

National solidarity, financed by French taxpayers, has made it possible to mitigate the increase in energy prices for everyone, safeguard our businesses, and particularly protect the incomes of the most modest among us. And thanks to our collective action, we supported growth, kept inflation at levels lower than those experienced by our neighbours, and brought unemployment down to its lowest level in fifteen years. Indeed, this year we continued to create jobs, and quality jobs.

With every challenge, Europe has enabled us to act faster and more forcefully: to build a united front of resistance against Russia, to reinvest in our industries, and above all to find, on the scale of the continent, responses to the challenges of our century. Thus, during the first six months of this year, when France held the Presidency of the Council of the European Union, we took decisions to reduce our greenhouse gas emissions by more than half by 2030; we agreed on a carbon tax at our borders to protect our industries and our planet; together, we decided to establish a minimum tax on large multinational corporations in order to combat tax evasion; and together, we began to regulate major digital platforms more effectively.

And despite all these crises and all these challenges, 2022 was also, for all of us, a year of intense democratic activity, during which you renewed our National Assembly and, in the presidential election this spring, decided to entrust me with a new five-year mandate at the head of our nation, an honour that also places obligations upon me.

2022 was also, once again, a year in which our country shone in the arts, culture and sport, with two Nobel Prizes and so many great moments of creativity and sporting achievement. Let us be proud of all this, and of everything we have accomplished together during the year that is now ending.

We must carry this pride and this confidence with us as we enter the year ahead. For I believe that 2023 will first of all be a year of questions that I know are causing concern, and of crises that we will once again have to confront.

Will we face electricity cuts? If we continue to save energy, as we have been doing for the past few months and as I announced to you as early as 14 July, and if we continue to bring our nuclear reactors back into service as planned, we will get through it. It is in our hands.

Will energy prices rise? Here too, we have put concrete responses in place. I say this to each and every one of you because, although energy prices have reached historic levels, increases will remain capped in our country. I say this in particular to our tradespeople, our bakers, but also to our most industrial businesses. Starting tomorrow, you will have tailored support in addition to the tariff shield already in place, so that the long-term survival of your businesses, our jobs and our competitiveness can be ensured. And whenever necessary, the Government will adapt its responses, as it has done at every stage. Above all, we will accelerate solutions that will enable us to free ourselves from our dependencies and establish an electricity price that reflects its actual cost of production.

Will we once again experience a wave of Covid, and will the epidemic ever end? Here too, we will be able to cope. First, thanks to the reasonable and appropriate use of the protective measures against the virus that we have learned. Second, thanks to vaccination, which has demonstrated its effectiveness; and this evening I particularly encourage all our fellow citizens over the age of 70 to receive their booster dose, or to get vaccinated if they have not already done so. Finally, by testing, sequencing and introducing border controls.

That is what the Government has decided to do in our airports starting tomorrow for flights arriving from China, where the epidemic is in full swing and where many restrictions have been lifted.

Will we have to work longer in 2023? Here too, as I pledged before you, this year will indeed be the year of a pension reform intended to ensure the balance of our system for the years and decades ahead. We need to work more. That is the very purpose of the unemployment insurance reform introduced by the Government and passed by Parliament. It is also the purpose of this reform, on which the social partners and the Government will work in the coming months in order to finalize the new rules that will apply from the end of the summer of 2023.

The objective is to strengthen our pay-as-you-go pension schemes, which without such measures would be threatened, because we continue to finance them through borrowing. To achieve this, the extension of our working lives will be gradual and will take place in stages over nearly ten years. It will also be fair, taking account of long careers, interrupted careers, and the difficulty of certain tasks and professions.

But this is what will enable us to balance the financing of our pensions in our country and, in a country where people are living longer—which is a fortunate thing—to improve the minimum pension for all those who have worked the required number of quarters, and to pass on to our children a social model that is fair and strong because it will be credible and sustainably financed.

Throughout the long history of our nation, there have been generations called upon to resist, others called upon to rebuild, and still others called upon to expand the prosperity that had been achieved.

As for us, it falls to us to confront this new chapter in a difficult era and, beyond the emergencies of this year, some of which I have just mentioned, to take responsibility for rebuilding many of the pillars of our nation, whether our schools, our healthcare system, our transport, the development of our regions, our industries, and many others.

To do this, we must remain united, but we must also preserve an undiminished collective ambition: an ambition to continue transforming our country in the face of vested interests, in the face of all the apparently good reasons for continuing as before, and in the face of the temptation to succumb to a spirit of defeat.

That is how we will serve our young people and the generations to come. Over the past five years, we have already done much of this work of transformation, simplification and overcoming inertia. But it is sometimes still too little, and too often too slow.

And like you, I too grow impatient, but without ever giving in to easy solutions or fatalism. And so my wish for us in 2023 is that, through our work and our commitment, we strive to rebuild a France that is stronger and fairer, so that we may pass it on to our children.

It is through our work and our commitment that we will be able to increase the resources of our domestic security forces, our justice system and our armed forces in the face of new geopolitical challenges and the multiplication of conflicts.

It is through our work and our commitment that we will fight more effectively against trafficking and against illegal immigration, both in mainland France and in our overseas territories. Let us always remain faithful to our values. Let us integrate people more effectively through language and work; let us protect the women and men who fight for freedom, such as those coming from Iran or elsewhere; but let us maintain control of our borders and preserve the unity of the nation.

It is through our work and our commitment that we will also build a productive and environmentally responsible nation. Because the ecological transition is a battle that we must win, we must pursue it with determination and method. Ecological planning will be the instrument of this historic transformation, enabling us to reduce our CO2 emissions and preserve our biodiversity. With our France 2030 plan, we will continue to invest, innovate and deploy environmental solutions on an industrial scale. And following the law intended to accelerate the development of renewable energy, the nuclear energy law will mark the beginning of the construction of new power plants on our territory.

It is through our work and our commitment that we will also restore a nation founded on trust. By making our secularism effective every day, because it is a principle of freedom. And it takes nothing away from the place of religion in each person’s private conscience, for all those who believe. At this moment, I pay tribute to the memory of His Holiness Benedict XVI, whose passing, I know, affects many Catholics in France and throughout the world.

This nation of trust will also be strengthened by an unwavering fight against all forms of discrimination, within a society founded on respect and recognition. It will also be reinforced by the daily struggle that we will continue to pursue in support of people with disabilities.

It is through our work and our commitment that we must rebuild our great public services so that they fully uphold our ideal of equality. Through the National Council for Refoundation, we have begun to renew the contract between generations and to work towards providing better support for our elderly citizens who are losing their independence.

We have also begun to restore confidence in our national education system and our healthcare system, drawing on the energy and dedication of our teachers and healthcare workers. We will pursue this work vigorously throughout the year ahead, through clear and strong choices and through action carried out as close as possible to the realities on the ground.

It is through our work and our commitment that we will build a fairer society. A fairer society is first and foremost one in which equality between women and men is a reality. This, which has been the great cause of both of my presidential terms, will continue to shape the Government’s work and inspire our actions every day.

But a fairer society is also one that is fairer socially. Not through higher taxes—no. Nor by leaving more debt to future generations. But by improving the support we provide to our children and adolescents, reforming vocational secondary education, and improving the guidance provided to our young people so that they can find the right training and the right careers.

By reindustrializing our country faster and more strongly, we will create new jobs and careers for the future. For the greatest injustice in our country remains the influence of family background and the weakness of social mobility. And the answer lies in schools, in career guidance, in higher education, in our innovation policy and in our industrialization.

And because confidence in the vitality of our democratic life has also weakened, we know that we will have much to do in the months ahead. In the coming weeks and months, I will lay the first foundations of a Universal National Service. We will have to initiate the necessary changes to our institutions and to our public and civic life. And together with the National Assembly and the Senate, as well as the Economic, Social and Environmental Council, we will have to build a better functioning of our institutions and involve our citizens more frequently.

France and Europe have an eminent role to play at this moment in the history of humanity, as so many authoritarian regimes challenge our democracies and their foundations. Protecting our children, protecting our free and independent information, protecting the free and just order that enables citizens to live happy lives: these are some of the struggles of our time.

We have a duty to take them on.

Yes, it is through our work and our commitment that we will give ourselves the means to fulfil our aspirations for today and our ambitions for tomorrow.

In short, in 2023, step by step, we will have to consolidate our energy, economic, social, industrial, financial and strategic independence, and strengthen what I might call our strength of spirit. This is what we owe to our children.

This is not, and never will be, a pursuit of illusions doomed from the outset. For French independence must find in Europe its extension and its complement. At a time when so many countries dream of becoming empires, and so many companies imagine themselves as kingdoms, we have a continent capable of forming an area of peace and freedom, prosperity, solidarity, law and power. Since 2017, we have pursued this struggle to bring Europe’s strengths together. So that, as 27 nations, we may be stronger.

That is why I have fought this battle in recent years, why you have heard me warn other Europeans as well about the need to defend our industries and our jobs following decisions taken on other continents a few weeks ago, and why I will redouble my efforts at the beginning of this year.

My dear fellow citizens,

Here and this evening, on your behalf, I want to say to our Ukrainian friends: we respect you and we admire you. Your struggle in defence of your nation is heroic, and it inspires us. And throughout the year ahead, we will stand unwaveringly by your side. We will help you until victory, and together we will work to build a just and lasting peace. You can count on France, and you can count on Europe.

As for us, let us be this generation of builders.

In the coming months of 2023, the reconstruction work on Notre-Dame de Paris, this extraordinary project, will move closer to completion. In the coming months, our entire country will come together in a spirit of fraternity as we approach the Olympic and Paralympic Games and as France hosts the Rugby World Cup. In the coming months, thanks to the France 2030 plan, the first electric cars built entirely on our territory will roll out of our factories.

And so many other projects will take shape throughout our country, enabling France both to reduce carbon emissions and to reduce unemployment. In the coming months, in our classrooms, in our hospitals and in our doctors’ practices, you will see the first tangible changes resulting from the renewal of our schools and our healthcare system.

For all of this, I wish for all of us unity, boldness, collective ambition and kindness. We have overcome so many crises together, my dear fellow citizens. I know that we are capable of overcoming those that lie ahead and of being the generation entrusted with the responsibility of rebuilding France and Europe so that we may pass them on to our children stronger, more beautiful and more just.

Together, we will succeed.

And it is with this confidence that I extend to all of you my very best wishes for the New Year.

Long live the Republic.

Long live France.

title: Vœux aux Français 2024
clean_text:
French women and men, in metropolitan France, in our overseas territories and abroad,

As I extend my best wishes to you, I want to begin by expressing our gratitude to all those among our fellow citizens who, once again this evening, are protecting, caring for others, helping, and ensuring the continuity of the life of the Nation. Thanks to them, we are able to spend these moments of transition from one year to the next with our families and loved ones. And at this moment, I also want to express my particular affection for those who are ill or who will remain alone.

The year 2023 was marked by the continuation of the war in Ukraine, the war now taking place in the Middle East and the bombardments of Gaza; by the terrorist attacks of October 7 in Israel, in which 41 French citizens were killed, and this evening my thoughts are with their families, just as they are with the families of our compatriots who are still being held hostage.

It was also marked by growing geopolitical tensions, by the consequences of climate disruption on our territory, and by acts of terrorism on our soil. By divisions, acts of hatred and, at times, violence on several occasions, which weaken the cohesion of the Nation. Finally, inflation has taken its toll, making everything more difficult: finding housing, getting around, doing the shopping.

There were, of course, happy moments, moments of pride, but I know how present the fear of the return of war, of decline, and of losing control remains.

And yet I am convinced—and this is not false optimism—that in this context of crises, the best can emerge.

That is why I have never ceased to follow the same course: to act with determination and consistency, for today and for tomorrow. For seven years, from the position in which you placed me, I have sought to make France stronger and fairer, to liberate, protect and unite. That is our course, and we are holding to it. And the same was true in 2023.

In 2023, France was undoubtedly one of the Western countries that, despite the circumstances, made the greatest number of decisions and carried out the greatest number of transformations. Some of them, such as the pension reform, were, I know, unpopular. I stand by them because I had committed to them and because they were necessary for the country.

All these past months have therefore been a far cry from the powerlessness that some had predicted for us, and that is a good thing. And I want here to thank especially the Prime Minister and her government.

In 2023, we acted—acted in pursuit of our goal of reindustrialisation and full employment, the first results of which are already visible. Pensions, unemployment insurance, the revival of our green industries, the acceleration of France 2030, the overhaul of vocational high schools, the reform of Pôle emploi and the active solidarity income, and the reform of the European electricity market: all these major transformations were decided upon, voted on, and began to take effect this year.

And this year we continued to create jobs while reducing our greenhouse gas emissions even more rapidly, in accordance with our commitments. This proves that you have risen to the challenge of this collective mobilisation.

Thanks to this economic strengthening, we remain able to finance our social model, to protect ourselves against crises or inflation, but also to invest in strengthening our public services. And that is what we have done.

We invested in our schools and our healthcare system in order to provide better support and better address inequalities of opportunity. We laid the foundations for an unprecedented ecological planning strategy and committed substantial resources to support each and every one of you through this transition.

In 2023, we also passed historic laws for the years ahead in order to protect ourselves. A historic law for our armed forces: over the course of a decade, the budget of our military will have doubled. A historic law for our police officers, gendarmes, magistrates and court clerks, in order to ensure public order and republican unity, including the creation of thousands of positions to better protect you. We will continue to restore authority wherever it is lacking in the face of antisocial behaviour and crime.

On immigration, the law passed in December, together with the agreement reached at the European level, gives us the tools necessary to better uphold the principles of the Republic: that is, both to fight smugglers and illegal immigration, and to better integrate those who are meant to remain on our soil—refugees, students, researchers and workers.

I am, of course, well aware of the impatience—and I would even venture to say that I share it—even though the first changes are already visible. I know that you would like us to do more and to do it faster. And it is to achieve this objective that 2024 must above all be a year of determination. To act, to act again, in the interest of the Nation.

We will be determined to act for schools, childhood and education, in order to restore the level of our pupils, the authority of our teachers, and the strength of our secular and republican education system. After strengthening our economy, strengthening the State and our public services, we must now undertake a civic strengthening of the Nation. France is a culture, a history, a language, universal values that must be learned from the earliest age. By every generation.

We will also be determined to make our Republic stronger by fighting crime, tackling discrimination more firmly, and enabling concrete progress toward equality between women and men, for early childhood, and for our fellow citizens with disabilities. We will be equally determined to intensify the strengthening of our industrial, technological and scientific capabilities. We must do everything we can to achieve our ambition of full employment, continue to innovate, but also attract talent and businesses and produce more in France. Accordingly, next year we will embark on major cutting-edge projects, from nuclear energy to artificial intelligence and transport. So that by 2027, we will be ten years ahead in areas where, in 2017, we were ten years behind.

In 2024, we will have to accelerate our efforts even further and radically simplify the lives of our entrepreneurs, farmers, shopkeepers, craftspeople, elected representatives—particularly our mayors—and many sectors, including housing.

Finally, we will be determined to act so that in 2024 our ecological approach—this distinctively French approach to ecology—and our planning continue to develop as a model and a unique path, allowing us to move away from fossil fuels and gain greater independence and progress. France, which already produces some of the least carbon-intensive electricity in Europe, will completely phase out coal by 2027. And we will pursue this same fight internationally, including through our Pact for People and the Planet.

2024: a year of determination, effectiveness and results. And in the weeks ahead, I will have the opportunity to explain to you how our Nation will meet these challenges.

My dear compatriots, action is not an option. Action is our duty toward future generations. That is why I will tirelessly stand with those who act in the service of the country, and never with those who refuse to tell you the truth in order to justify doing nothing and who, in the end, weaken us. Never with those who put electoral calculations, petty arrangements or their personal interests first.

We must therefore continue strengthening the Nation in the face of the disorder of the world. For strength of character is the virtue required in difficult times.

2024 will also be a year of decisive choices.

We will have to choose a stronger, more sovereign Europe, in light of the legacy of Jacques Delors. A Europe that works for peace in the Middle East and on our own continent, by continuing to support the Ukrainian people and, with them, our security, our freedom and our values. Next June, you will be called upon to decide whether to continue strengthening our European sovereignty in the face of these dangers: whether to stop Russia and support the Ukrainians, or give way to authoritarian powers in Ukraine; whether to continue building Europe or bring it to a halt; whether to continue the ecological and productive transition or turn back; whether to affirm the strength of liberal democracies or give way to the lies that sow chaos.

Finally, 2024 will be a year of French pride. Pride in the thousands of craftsmen, builders and entrepreneurs who have taken part in the magnificent project to rebuild Notre-Dame de Paris, whose spire once again rises toward the sky above a cathedral that will reopen on December 8.

We are a Nation of builders and craftspeople, capable, when united, of resisting and rising again. Yes, in five years, as promised, we will have rebuilt the cathedral and accomplished the impossible. We are that Nation which, when proud of itself, always carries a universal hope.

In 2024, we will also celebrate our History. Eighty years after 1944, we will take pride in our past and in our heroes whose destinies became intertwined. Soldiers of the Allied armies, but also French citizens by birth or by choice, French and foreign members of the Resistance. All fighting so that a France faithful to the spirit of the Enlightenment and to the spirit of our Revolution could be liberated.

2024 will be a year of pride in the French language. After restoring the Château de Villers-Cotterêts and creating there the Cité internationale de la langue française, in a few months we will welcome the French-speaking world there.

2024 will also be a year of French sporting pride, as the Olympic and Paralympic Games will take place here, in France, and therefore, in a sense, at home for all of us, both in metropolitan France and in our overseas territories.

We will be proud of our athletes, our artists, our landscapes, and of this great popular celebration, made possible by thousands of volunteers, who will also build a sporting legacy for our Nation. Through the commitment of us all, beginning tomorrow.

Yes, 2024 will, as you have understood, be a truly French vintage year. Because it is only once every decade that we commemorate our Liberation on such a scale. It is only once a century that we host the Olympic and Paralympic Games. And it is only once in a millennium that we rebuild a cathedral. It is only once in a generation that the destiny of the next is decided, as it undoubtedly is being decided now.

2024: a year of determination, choices, renewal and pride. At its heart, a year of hope. Yes, much of our future will be decided this year. So it is up to us to act together. It is up to us to choose rather than endure, to chart the course rather than follow it.

And our entire History teaches us that the determination of a few can overcome every seeming inevitability. So it is up to us to act—yes, to act together, to continue to move beyond divisions and narrow group interests, because within our people lie the deep reserves of strength needed to meet these challenges.

My dear compatriots, I wish you a very beautiful and very happy year 2024.

So that France may unite, act and shine. May it be worthy of the “indefinable splendour of those who are destined for great undertakings,” because that is who we are.

Long live the Republic. Long live France.

title: Vœux aux Français 2025
clean_text:
My dear compatriots,

Together, this year, we proved that “impossible” is not a French word.

We became the first nation to amend our Constitution in order to guarantee women’s right to voluntarily terminate a pregnancy. We advanced equality between women and men, among other things thanks to the courage of those who dared to speak out.

We continued to build an ecology based on progress, to fight climate change by reducing our emissions, by opening factories, and by continuing to fight for both our present and our future.

We commemorated the bravery of our Resistance fighters and of those who liberated us, 80 years later, from Normandy to Provence.

We remembered those who fell so that France could rise again. Our heroes, our elders, our allies, those who came from every continent to liberate our homeland.

We also experienced, as I promised a year ago, moments of great pride. First of all, this summer we organized Olympic and Paralympic Games that immediately entered history, entered our memories and our hearts, that made a united country come alive, from Saint-Denis to Tahiti, and showed a France full of boldness, flair and extraordinary freedom.

A France that shines through its sporting achievements, its emotions, its generosity, and through a city of Paris shown at its very best.

Our Olympic and Paralympic Games, yes, are and will remain an unforgettable moment in the life of the Nation.

In this month of December 2024, as we had promised, we returned Notre-Dame de Paris to worship and reopened it to the public. Five years after the fire of 2019, the rebuilt Notre-Dame remains a symbol of our French determination.

Thousands of workers, craftsmen, women and men rebuilt the cathedral day after day throughout those five years. It was returned to everyone, and the entire world was able to admire this work.

Tomorrow, let us know how to preserve the best of what we were during this year, 2024. United, determined and in solidarity, and in the face of every major ordeal, in the face of what so many people said was impossible, we succeeded because we stood together.

United, determined and in solidarity, we also stood together in the face of the trials and tragedies of 2024: climate-related disasters, the crisis our farmers are still experiencing today, whom we will continue to protect and support, tensions in several of our territories, and the global economic slowdown.

Together, today we stand alongside the people of Mayotte, whom we are thinking of with emotion and solidarity. And of course, we are and will remain alongside all of our overseas territories, from the Antilles to New Caledonia, which has suffered so greatly in recent months.

We are also confronted with political instability. It is not unique to France; we also see it among our German friends, who have just dissolved their Parliament. But it legitimately concerns us.

I must acknowledge this evening that, for the moment, the dissolution has brought more divisions to the National Assembly than solutions for the French people.

If I decided to dissolve the Assembly, it was to give you back your voice, to restore clarity and to avoid the paralysis that threatened us. But lucidity and humility require us to recognize that, at this point, this decision has produced more instability than calm, and I fully accept my share of responsibility for it.

The current Assembly nevertheless represents the country in all its diversity, and therefore also in its divisions. It is fully legitimate, and in this unprecedented but democratic configuration, it must be capable of forming majorities, as parliaments in the great democracies do, and our government must be able to follow a path of compromise in order to act.

I would like to thank Michel Barnier here, who, after Elisabeth Borne and Gabriel Attal, committed himself with sincerity, and I extend my very best wishes to François Bayrou and his government.

I hope that the year ahead will be one of collective recovery, that it will bring stability and the right compromises needed to make the right decisions in the service of the French people.

Because we cannot afford to wait. The year 2025 must be a year of action, a useful year for you and one that enables you to live better. Purchasing power, employment, security, justice, and support for our elected representatives and our associations: for all of these things, it is necessary to adopt a budget.

We can make life better by agreeing on a few simple matters: making life easier for all those who work hard, improving everyday security, delivering justice more quickly, and enabling every family to have access to the best education for their children, to healthcare, and to basic public services. It is therefore up to us to do this.

The year 2025 must also be a year of unity and responsibility, in order to build a stronger and more independent France in the face of the world’s upheavals.

The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East are not distant conflicts. They concern us directly and threaten our security, our unity and our economy.

Recent events in Syria, the manipulation of elections in Moldova, Georgia and Romania, and terrorist attacks in Europe and in our neighboring regions show just how much our security and the proper functioning of our democracies can never be taken for granted.

That is why Europe can no longer delegate its security and defense to other powers. In 2025, France must continue investing in its military rearmament in order to guarantee our sovereignty, the protection of our interests, and the security of our fellow citizens. Europe, for its part, must accelerate its efforts to take control of its own defense, security and borders. This is what I have been fighting for for so many years, what we have begun to build with our European partners, and what we will continue to pursue.

We must clearly recognize that the world is moving faster and challenging many of our certainties. What we once took for granted can no longer be taken for granted.

There can be no prosperity without security, and France, through its diplomatic and military power, still has a role to play in this respect.

If our children are to live better than we do, the technologies and companies that will shape the world of tomorrow, our future and our growth, must also be developed in France and in Europe: artificial intelligence, the revolutions in quantum technologies, energy and biology, to name only a few of these fields.

Europeans must put an end to their naivety. We must say no to trade rules dictated by others that we are the only ones still respecting, and say no to everything that makes us dependent on others without anything in return and without preparing for our future.

On the contrary, what we need is a European awakening: a scientific, intellectual, technological and industrial awakening, as well as an agricultural, energy and ecological awakening. To achieve this, we must move faster, make our decisions more rapidly and more decisively as Europeans, simplify our rules for our fellow citizens as well as for our businesses, and invest more.

This requires a France that continues to be attractive, that works and innovates more, that continues to create jobs and that ensures its growth while keeping its public finances under control. I will see to it.

For seven years, we have managed to withstand the worst crises while reducing unemployment, reindustrializing the country and attracting innovations from all over the world.

Once again this year, we demonstrated our ability to maintain our standing in sectors of the future, with, for example, the launch of Ariane 6 and the connection of the new Flamanville nuclear reactor to the grid. This is where our independence is being built, and we must remain strong and credible at the heart of a Europe that must accelerate.

It is therefore up to all of us, collectively, to act, because 2025 will demand boldness and decisiveness.

My dear compatriots, great nations are those that, in moments of crisis and doubt, know how to look far ahead, rise above the controversies of everyday life, build the future and stay one step ahead.

This is where we are today. That is why, in 2025, we will stay the course.

We are now a quarter of a century into this century. Some of the promises of the year 2000 have been fulfilled, but so many disruptions and imbalances have also emerged. So, for the quarter-century ahead, I want us to be able to decide and act, with 2050 in our sights.

We will have choices to make for our economy, our democracy, our security and our children. Yes, the hope, prosperity and peace of the quarter-century ahead depend on the choices we make today.

That is why, in 2025, we will continue to make decisions, and I will also ask you to decide on some of these decisive issues. Because each and every one of you will have a role to play. Each and every one of you will be necessary if we are to succeed in the project I have just briefly outlined before you. Yes, just as with the great undertakings that have shaped our history, and again during the year that has just passed, each and every one of you is necessary to build an even greater Nation and Republic.

That is why, for 2025, I wish for all of us to remain united, determined and fraternal.

I wish you and your loved ones a wonderful and very happy year 2025.

Long live the Republic.

Long live France.

title: Vœux aux Français 2026
clean_text:
French women and men, my dear compatriots,

On this evening of December 31, my thoughts go first and foremost to those who ensure the continuity of the Nation: the security forces, firefighters, volunteers, healthcare workers, workers, and all those who, tonight as always, are on the front line in the face of hardship. Protecting, caring, feeding, helping, providing assistance and solidarity—this is how great nations endure each day, through the dedication of their citizens. On behalf of all of you, my thoughts are with those who are alone, ill, facing hardship or deprivation. I know how difficult the situation is for many of you, confronted with personal suffering and the hardships of life, and I want to express our support and affection.

Thanks to everyone’s commitment, thanks to you, we are holding firm. Yes, our country is holding firm. Strong in its institutions and its public services; strong in its armed forces, which are the most effective in Europe, thanks to the commitment of its soldiers. Strong in our economy, where never before have so many French people been employed, where growth remains steady, and where our inflation is among the lowest in the euro area. Strong in our research, our academic excellence, and also in our diplomatic initiatives, whether those undertaken for peace, the climate, or our oceans.

But beyond all this, no one is blind to the disorder in the world or to our own weaknesses. Our world is becoming harsher every day. War and instability persist in the Near and Middle East, with consequences for our economies, our interests, and sometimes our cohesion. And war continues to rage on European soil, with particular intensity since Russia decided to launch a new aggression against Ukraine nearly four years ago. We are witnessing the return of empires, the questioning of the international order, a world of trade wars, technological competition, and often instability.

I also see our own divisions, our doubts, the growing loneliness within society, the decline in our birth rate, insecurity, and difficulties with purchasing power.

I know all the impatience, and sometimes the anger, that continues to exist in the country, and I share several of those concerns. These urgent matters require answers. From the very first weeks of the year ahead, the Government and Parliament will have to build agreements in order to provide the nation with a budget. This is essential. From the beginning of 2026, we will need to act: to support our farmers in the face of crises and protect them from decisions that could threaten our ability to produce, as well as our food security. To further strengthen our economy by simplifying the rules for our entrepreneurs as well as for our farmers. To persevere in our efforts against insecurity and all forms of antisocial behaviour, and to relentlessly combat drug trafficking in all its forms. To continue regaining control of our French and European borders in the face of illegal immigration; to continue training our teachers and give primary and lower secondary schools the means to better transmit fundamental knowledge; to recognise the expertise of our doctors, both in community care and in hospitals, by simplifying the way they work and allowing them greater freedom to make decisions and organise their activities. To implement concrete and radical decentralisation, developed together with our local elected representatives, in order to simplify the functioning of the country, make savings, and at the same time respond to the legitimate aspirations of Corsica and several overseas territories. For all of this—and I could have listed here every project that lies ahead of us—I know that the Government is hard at work and that the Prime Minister is determined to be of service to the country, and tonight I want to thank them sincerely for that. This will also require everyone’s mobilisation and the efforts of all.

This year, municipal elections will also be held in our towns and communities. And tonight I want once again to express to all our mayors and elected representatives my recognition and gratitude. Over the past few years, they have stood with me through every struggle and every crisis, serving you.

This year must therefore be, and will be, a useful year.

I will pay particular attention to ensuring that several major projects are brought to completion. We will see the first steps of the national service programme for the engagement of our young people, which will strengthen the bond between our armed forces and the nation. We will protect our children and adolescents from social media and screens. And we will finally bring the legislative process concerning the question of a dignified end of life to completion, an issue on which I made a commitment to you in 2022.

At the end of the year, when the time comes, the next campaign for the 2027 presidential election will gradually begin—the first presidential election in ten years in which I will not take part. Nevertheless, until the very last second, I will remain at work, striving every day to live up to the mandate you entrusted to me, and I will do everything possible to ensure that the presidential election takes place as calmly as possible, and in particular free from any foreign interference.

Beyond the work that must be done, I have three wishes for our nation.

First, a wish for unity. Whatever the challenges, our history teaches us that we can overcome anything and face anything if we know how to remain united. Let us therefore never forget that the reasons we have for living together are, every day, stronger than whatever may divide us, stronger than the flood of emergencies, individual incidents, or bad news. Our unity requires us to fight relentlessly against antisemitism, racism, and every form of discrimination. Our unity requires us to recognise that every French woman and every French man has a role to play in meeting the challenges ahead of us, that each and every one of us is necessary and deserves encouragement and recognition. Yes, in our everyday lives, ultimately, I wish for us to show greater kindness and greater humanity.

My second wish is a wish for strength and independence. At a time when the law of the strongest is attempting to impose itself on world affairs and our Europe is under pressure from every side, we must defend our independence and our freedoms.

Our independence requires us to continue investing in our armed forces, our security forces, our public services, and our economy despite financial difficulties. For ten years, I have argued strongly for this independence, and as Europeans we have done a great deal to strengthen it, but now we must accelerate. European defence was for a long time merely a subject of debate; it has now begun to take shape, and in 2026 this process will accelerate. As early as January 6, in Paris, many European states and allies will make concrete commitments to protect Ukraine and secure a just and lasting peace on our European continent. Let us also protect our industrial and agricultural Europe by establishing fair and equitable trade rules in relation to the rest of the world. Let us dare to become a true power, one that embraces a European preference for its jobs and its businesses. Let us build an independent Europe in the space industry, quantum technologies, and artificial intelligence. Our prosperity, both in France and across Europe, depends on it.

My final wish is a wish for hope—hope for ourselves and for our children.

Let us not give up. Let us not give up on progress, which is still possible provided that we build it, work hard, invest for the long term, and recognise that genuine progress does not happen in a single day, but sometimes takes the span of a generation.

Let us not give up on reconciling the climate, biodiversity, growth, and independence. Let us not give up on major scientific discoveries, on our love of science and research, or on economic success.

Let us not give up on the place of reading, beauty, and culture. Let us not give up, day after day, on becoming a nation that is more supportive and more fraternal. Yes, ultimately, I wish for us to resist the spirit of the times, quite simply because we are French. We must stand firm in defending what we cherish: humanity, peace, and freedom. We will succeed. So let us look ahead, and let us look far into the future, as citizens and as a nation.

My dear compatriots in mainland France, in our overseas territories, and living abroad, I wish you a wonderful and very happy year 2026.

Long live the Republic! Long live France!

title: Neujahrsansprache 2017
clean_text:
Dear fellow citizens,

2016 was a year of severe trials. I would like to speak to you about that this evening — but also about why, despite everything, I remain confident about Germany and why I am so deeply convinced of the strengths of our country and its people.

The most serious challenge is, without doubt, Islamist terrorism, which has also had us Germans in its sights for many years. In 2016, it struck us in the heart of our own country: in Würzburg, in Ansbach, and only a few days ago at the Christmas market here at the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church in Berlin.

And — yes — it is especially bitter and repugnant when terrorist attacks are committed by people who supposedly seek protection in our country. People who, precisely for that reason, have experienced the willingness of our country to help them and who now mock that generosity through their actions. Just as they also mock those who genuinely need and deserve our protection.

So what, then, of the confidence I spoke of at the beginning?

Confidence in the midst of deep grief for the dead and the injured?
